# Regression Model:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
model_ic <- lm(priceper1 ~ household_income + household_size + married,
               data = ice_cream)

summary(model_ic)
```

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# The regression results show that household income, household size, and marital status are all statistically significant predictors of ice cream price per unit. Higher household income is associated with slightly lower price per unit, suggesting that higher-income households may purchase larger or discounted packages. Similarly, larger households pay about $0.02 less per unit for each additional household member, indicating bulk purchasing behavior. Married households pay about $0.069 less per unit than non-married households, holding other factors constant. Although all predictors are statistically significant, the R-squared is very low (0.0087), and it suggests that other factors not included in the model likely to play a much larger role in determining price per unit.
```
